key_insight: A 2026 public charge rule could reduce immigrants’ use of primary care in NYC and, over time, increase premature mortality through a chilling effect on coverage and care access.
clinical_relevance: Health systems and clinicians serving immigrant communities should anticipate potential declines in coverage uptake and care use, with disproportionate harms among legal noncitizens and Black immigrant New Yorkers.
method: Deterministic compartmental simulation using ordinary differential equations.
Calibrated with 2023 NYC vital statistics and American Community Survey data.
Applied effect estimates from prior studies linking healthcare access to primary care use and premature mortality.
evidence_signal: Model projections compared conservative, moderate, and aggressive chilling-effect scenarios against counterfactuals, estimating changes in primary care outcomes over 5 years and premature mortality over 5 and 20 years.
watch_item: Because this is a simulation based on prior effect estimates, results depend on the assumptions behind the chilling-effect scenarios and may not capture all real-world policy responses.
paper_title: The 2026 public charge rule and long-term health impacts among NYC immigrants: a simulation study
